sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2016. Mayan phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 10(10): 469-514. doi:10.1111/lnc3.12148 (author's open copy)
sources.quote: p. 495: 'Final stress (36a) is the norm in K'ichean languages'. p. 497: Berinstein (1979) shows stress in Kaqchikel and Q'eqchi' is cued by raised pitch and amplitude; duration a cue in Kaqchikel but not Q'eqchi' because vowel length is phonemic only in Q'eqchi'. No Q'eqchi'-specific statement of stress position beyond the K'ichean generalization.

sources.citation: Wagner, Karl Olaw Christian. 2014. An Intonational Description of Mayan Q'eqchi'. M.A. thesis, Brigham Young University. 139 pp. Open: https://scholarsarchive.byu.edu/etd/4151/
sources.quote: p. 29: 'Q'eqchi' has fixed word-final stress with very few exceptions (Stewart, 1980)'; a few Spanish borrowings retain non-final stress; Kockelman's interjection uyaluy has initial stress. p. 43: 'Stress always fell on the last syllable of content words... consistently found on the final syllable of content words such as verbs, nouns, adjectives, and adverbs' (3 male speakers, 75 sentences each, pitch rise on final syllable). p. 44: 'this leaves non-final syllables of content words, clitics, articles, and other function words unstressed' (quotative enclitic chan unstressed). p. 71-72: stress

sources.citation: Berinstein, Ava E. 1979. A cross-linguistic study on the perception and production of stress. UCLA Working Papers in Phonetics 47 (M.A. thesis). Open: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/0t0699hc
sources.quote: 'Both K'ekchi and Cakchiquel have fixed final stress but they differ in that while K'ekchi has phonemic vowel length, Cakchiquel does not.' (p. vi); 'the Mayan language K'ekchi (fixed final stress). In K'ekchi, there is also phonemic vowel length.' (p. 5). Production/perception result: stressed syllables higher in F0 and amplitude but not longer; duration is not a stress cue in K'ekchi.
sources.locator: p. vi (abstract; PDF p. 10) and Ch. 2 sec. 2.2 'Subjects' (printed p. 5; PDF p. 15); speakers from Cobán, Alta Verapaz
